title: Every altar is also sanctified in honor of God, Mary, and all Saints—beyond any single tomb-ratio
source_text: XXIV. Ubi observandum est altare quodlibet sanctificari quidem in nomen & memoriam singularis alicujus Sancti, a quo suam accipit denominationem, & cujus respectu poterit habere rationem tumuli, ut loquitur Bellarminus: Verum omnia & singula altaria sanctificari praeterea, non tantum in honorem Dei omnipotentis, sed & in honorem Virginis Mariae, ac omnium Sanctorum, ad quos nihil pertinet ratio illa tumuli, sub qua solum licitum est, ex nuper allata Bellarmini doctrina, altaria Sanctis dedicari.
pass_a_gloss: Where it is to be observed that any altar whatever is indeed sanctified in the name and memory of some singular Saint, from whom it takes its denomination, and with respect to whom it will be able to have the reason of a tumulus, as Bellarmine speaks: But yet all and each altars are sanctified besides, not only in honor of almighty God, but also in honor of the Virgin Mary, and of all the Saints, to whom that reason of a tumulus does not at all pertain, under which alone it is lawful, by Bellarmine’s doctrine just alleged, to dedicate altars to the Saints.
pass_b_english: Each altar gets a title Saint (possible tomb-ratio)—and also a general sanctification to God, Mary, and all Saints.
That universal honor outruns Bellarmino’s tumulus-only leave.

lemmas.latin: in honorem Virginis Mariae, ac omnium Sanctorum
lemmas.gloss: in honor of the Virgin Mary and of all the Saints

choices.why: Universal extra dedication beyond the title Saint.
